existing.description_short: RSF Press Freedom Index: US Drops to 57th, Behind Sierra Leone
existing.description_long: On May 2, 2025, Reporters Without Borders (RSF) published its annual World Press Freedom Index, ranking the United States 57th out of 180 countries — a decline of 2 places from 2024 and 13 places from 2023, placing the US one spot behind Sierra Leone. RSF noted 'an alarming deterioration in press freedom' under Trump's second term and cited 'an authoritarian shift in government,' including weaponized institutions, defunding of independent media, and sidelining of reporters. The US social indicator score dropped 28 places, and the economic indicator fell 14 points over two years. The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) issued a simultaneous warning urging newsrooms to form a united front against the 'rising tide of threats.' The RSF noted that over 60% of journalists surveyed in Arizona, Florida, Nevada, and Pennsylvania said it was 'difficult to earn a living wage as a journalist.'

input.original_title: Trump Coerces States with Federal Funding Tied to Policy Compliance

existing.title: Trump Coerces States with Federal Funding Tied to Policy Compliance
existing.description_short: Trump Coerces States with Federal Funding Tied to Policy Compliance
existing.description_long: Beginning in early 2025 and escalating through August 2025, the Trump administration and DOGE systematically attached unprecedented conditions to federal grants and withheld congressionally appropriated funds to coerce states into compliance with immigration enforcement, DEI elimination, and other White House priorities. In February 2025, the Education Department and DOGE gave states 14 days to eliminate all DEI programs or face funding revocation. DOGE employees seized control of Grants.gov and inserted new approval layers, blocking NIH from publishing normal funding opportunities — only three NOFOs between January 20 and March 26, 2025, compared to 163 in 2023. On August 7, 2025, Trump signed an executive order inserting political appointees into all federal grant review processes. Courts repeatedly blocked these conditions as violating the Constitution's Spending Clause. More than 30 local governments won a federal injunction in April 2025 blocking conditions on $4 billion in federal grants.

input.original_title: ICE Detains and Deports U.S. Citizens and Green Card Holders by Mistake

existing.title: ICE Detains and Deports U.S. Citizens and Green Card Holders by Mistake
existing.description_short: ICE Detains and Deports U.S. Citizens and Green Card Holders by Mistake
existing.description_long: Throughout 2025, a pattern of ICE mistakenly detaining U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents emerged across the country. In May 2025, U.S.-born Florida native Leonardo Garcia Venegas, 25, was wrestled to the ground at his Alabama construction site and cuffed after agents called his Real ID 'fake.' Hugo Monteiro, a 31-year-old Brazilian-American U.S. citizen since 2020, was taken from outside a Cambridge, Massachusetts courthouse by ICE agents who confused him with a wanted person. By September 2025, seven American citizens and one green card holder filed joint legal claims alleging wrongful detention and racial profiling; some alleged they were beaten by federal agents. DHS announced it was on pace to deport nearly 600,000 undocumented immigrants by end of 2025. In October, Frank Miranda, a California-born U.S. citizen, was held for hours at a Portland ICE building by plainclothes masked agents who told him he was 'on an overstay.'
